source.title: Training-Free Pretrained Model Merging
source.authors: Zhenxing Xu; Ke Yuan; Hui-Qiong Wang; Yong Wang; Ming-Li Song; Jie Song

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares unit similarity in weight and activation spaces and reports that they can disagree, refining the claim that representation similarity is captured consistently by a single measure. It does not test whether alignment increases with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The focal result is the Fig. 1 unit-similarity experiment. The paper's many merged-model accuracy results evaluate downstream merging performance, not representation convergence itself, so they are not recorded as rows. The stated use of CIFAR-10 data and selection of a balance factor do not establish convergence across inputs or scales.
record.test_reason: This is a model-merging paper that uses unit matching as a tool and reports mainly its own method's merged-model accuracy. The Fig. 1 experiment compares weight-space and activation-space Pearson similarity of units. Its two parents are one CIFAR-10 ResNet-50 and a copy with only the 5th conv layer retrained. It does not measure convergence between independently trained models, and weight similarity is not a representational-similarity metric of the kind V6 concerns. So it measures a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that unit similarity in weight space and activation space is inconsistent. They find that MuDSC, which linearly combines both similarity matrices, improves merged multi-task models across tasks and architectures. Loss-landscape visualization places the merged model in overlapping low-loss regions.
record.recipe_differences: The focal experiment uses Pearson similarity to compare weight and activation spaces; the proposed MuDSC combines these spaces for unit matching. It is not a reproduction of the original representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight-space and activation-space similarity yield different assessments of unit pairs in the tested layer.

fits_no_version.finding: In one ResNet-50 layer, many unit pairs have highly similar weights but very different activations. The best merged unit's parents are similar in both spaces (Fig. 1, S1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space and activation-space unit similarity can disagree, and this choice affects which units are matched for merging.

record.problems: The focal similarity evidence is qualitative and figure-based, with no uncertainty reported for that result. It concerns one layer of one model under one stated data setting, not convergence across model scales, modalities, or input distributions.
record.rows_left_out: Merged-model accuracy results in Tables 1–4 and supplementary tables are downstream task-performance comparisons, not direct measurements of representation convergence or interchangeability. Values used to select the MuDSC balance factor are also not convergence outcomes.

untested.parts: No measure of shared features or subspaces across seeds. Merging seed-different ResNet20s reports only task accuracy.
Permutation merging accuracy is reported, but not representation mapping loss, stitching or relative representations.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Similarity measures, neighbour settings and inputs for cross-model representational convergence are not varied.
No test of plateau or causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Convergent Learning (arXiv:1511.07543) only as motivation. The merged-model accuracies in Tables 1-4 and S1-S7 are method-performance comparisons, so excluding them as rows is correct. Merged models from randomly initialized ResNet20s fall well below ensembles, for example joint accuracy 56.01 vs 69.51 on CIFAR100. This could loosely interest V4, but the models were trained on different class subsets and only task accuracy is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, nor comparison of independently trained models' representation alignment as they grow.
No paired image-caption vision-language alignment experiment.
Models are trained separately in some experiments, but the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
The study uses unit matching and parameter merging, but does not directly measure whether one model's representations can be mapped onto another's with little loss.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.

Tests disagreement between weight- and activation-space similarity in one ResNet-50 layer setting; does not vary neighbour count, compare out-of-distribution inputs, or broadly test other similarity settings.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; the 5th convolution layer was then retrained
rows.operation_detail: Compared weight-space and activation-space similarity for pairwise combinations of units, and examined the similarity of merged units to their parents.
rows.measure: Weight-space similarity versus activation-space similarity between parent units; the figure also depicts the smaller activation similarity between each merged unit and its two parents.
rows.value: The text reports many pairs with highly similar weights but very different activation values; the best merged unit has parents that are highly similar in both spaces. Figure values are not reported numerically.
rows.note: The paper describes the plotted qualitative result in the text. The similarity comparison shows that the choice of representation space changes which units appear similar.
rows.check: The parents are not independently trained models: the second is the first with only the 5th conv layer retrained. The comparison is weight-space versus activation-space unit similarity, used to motivate a merging criterion. It is not the dependence of measured representational convergence on metric settings or inputs. No numbers are given, only a figure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-50, 5th convolution layer, CIFAR-10 unit pairs
reader_labels.reason: Weight and activation similarity can disagree for the same unit pairs, while the reported best merged unit has high similarity in both spaces (r1). The result supports dependence on the similarity measure in this setting.
